name: Tama (Colombia)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Tucanoan lang; only Ortiz 1965 (wordlist-grade) and Ramirez 2019 classification refs; no phonological description found

sources.citation: Cook, Dorothy M. & Frances L. Gralow. 1977/1984. Fonología del coreguaje. In Sistemas fonológicos de idiomas colombianos 3. Bogotá: ILV. (Rosetta Project copy rosettaproject_coe_phon-1 on archive.org)
sources.note: Closest described variety (Koreguaje, kore1283, already catalogued); if Tama is a Koreguaje dialect its accent/tone statement would apply by proxy. Archive.

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid page tama1340; Wikipedia 'Tama language (Colombia)'; Crossref records for 10.2307/j.ctv16zjj4d(.1-.15) and 10.25100/peu.5599628; ORCID 0000-0001-6800-8242 works list
sources.note: Used to identify the two Mora works and the 2019 book's chapter structure; ORCID lists no thesis or separate tone/accent article by the author.

sources.citation: Mora Cortés, Luis Emilio. 1992. La dominancia nasal en la variedad tama. Forma y Función 6: 91-102. Bogotá: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Departamento de Lingüística. (Glottolog ref 703968, listed by Glottolog as a minimal description)
sources.note: Read in full (12 pp., text): treats only distinctive nasality and nasal harmony in the Tama variety (data collected 1990-91 in Koreguaje communities Maticurú and Buenos Aires); gives a consonant/vowel phoneme chart (p. 101) but says nothing about stress, accent or tone. Acute marks appear on some vowels in transcriptions (e.g. /káamɨ/ 'cuello', /húɨka/ 'enfermo', p. 96) but are never explained. p. 91: 'El propósito es determinar si lo que se conoce como "tama" es una lengua, o una variante dialectal del koreguaje.'

sources.citation: Mora Cortés, Luis Emilio. 2019. Cap. 6 'Análisis fonológico de los datos de tama' (pp. 69-96, incl. 'La combinatoria de los fonemas: la sílaba' p. 94) and Conclusiones (pp. 119-122), same book.
